review: Read the complete player panel and test, the unchanged minecraftPlayJourney helper and final production diff. First-party React/TypeScript; mocked authority, pairing and loopback receipts. No runtime profiles, credentials, game assets, private transcripts or third-party source copied.

Explicit Play verifies an exact chat binding, current room/source/player and finite capability review, then uses separate native startup and private pairing before dispatching the displayed objective. Pickup acknowledgement is distinguished from goal/monitor readiness and game execution.

The current preset selects registered player capabilities for a finite two-hour lease with manual-input cancellation. The displayed capability set, confirmation and server authority remain separate from chat pairing. Owner controls, bounded review drafts and armed emergency stop retain their existing roles.

Post-R379 identity isolation remounts setup state when account, chat, room, world, environment, subject or source changes. Scoped fetches reject late headers/JSON; every asynchronous activation boundary checks the same cancellation signal before another request or steering.

Tests cover six identity/unmount changes during chat inspection plus late authority, launch and pairing responses. Existing tests cover exact finite scope, independent pairing, heartbeat readiness, preserved unsaved choices and serialized polling.

The unchanged journey helper separates prerequisite stages and creates visible bounded steering context; it does not grant authority or execute actions. Existing policy and startup modules were separately reviewed. Shared schemas, live native services and remaining dependencies retain their own qualification.
limits: Unfrozen unpublished source proposal, not a standalone application or public release.
The identity-isolation change is newer than R379 and awaits installed testing.
Canceling UI continuation does not cancel or undo a backend operation already admitted. Backend identity, consent and lease enforcement remains independent.
HTTP and steering receipts are mocked; source tests do not establish two-player consent, live server/client readiness, Minecraft actions or GPT Live continuity.
